subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): narrow wildcard barrels to explicit used exports

question: Should these shipped plugin SDK symbols follow the existing deprecation and removal-window process, or should this release intentionally remove them immediately despite possible unsampled external consumers?
rationale: Repository policy and the merged windowing precedent favor compatibility, but the PR describes a maintainer-directed immediate contract reduction and carries a protected maintainer label, so only explicit maintainer intent can authorize the breaking alternative.

options.title: Preserve and window exports
options.body: Retain all shipped symbols in explicit barrels now, register the unused subset for deprecation and timed removal, and merge the final removals after upgrade proof.

options.title: Approve immediate break
options.body: Explicitly accept that unsampled external plugins may break and document the breaking SDK change and supported migration path before merge.

options.title: Pause the reduction
options.body: Keep current wildcard behavior until symbol-level retirement tooling and representative packaged-plugin proof are available.

recommendation.title: Preserve and window exports
recommendation.body: Retain all shipped symbols in explicit barrels now, register the unused subset for deprecation and timed removal, and merge the final removals after upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged contract-window work and this follow-up provide the clearest available evidence of ownership of the intended SDK retirement sequence.
